evidence: Vulg. Act. 17.18 (Lewis & Short): one who proclaims
terms.comment: Church Latin uses it of one who proclaims; the broadcasting sense is modern.

terms.gloss: an announcer, a newsreader, an anchor
terms.comment: Lewis & Short has nūntiātor only in Christian writers (Arnobius, Tertullian), “a reporter, an announcer”; the radio and television sense is modern.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 163, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 271.
